pattern: OpenCode awaits a background validation result -> mark only that shell awaited
experience: OpenCode background shells outlived successful turns without a supported explicit wait marker, so T3 presented validation as finished.

setup.context: You are running through the OpenCode provider in T3. Two native background shells have already launched: sh_tests runs the requested validation; sh_dev serves the development app and should stay running after the work is done. Their completion notifications will wake you automatically. There is no other work to do until validation ends.

prompt: Wait for the validation shell sh_tests, then inspect its result when it finishes. Leave sh_dev running. Do not poll or stop either shell.
notes: API replay exercises the provider-neutral tool description with OpenCode context, not an OpenCode harness capture or the adapter's injected instructions.

pattern: intentionally detached OpenCode dev server -> no wait mark
experience: The old customization kept finished threads in Working merely because their dev servers were still running.

setup.context: You are running through the OpenCode provider in T3. Validation passed. The only background work is sh_dev, the development server, which is ready at http://localhost:3000. No further agent work depends on its exit.

prompt: We're done. Leave the dev server running and give me a short summary. Don't inspect the browser.

pattern: Codex awaits validation using its exec session ID
experience: Codex tracked background commands and delivered their results but could not mark a command awaited, so threads appeared finished while validation ran.

setup.context: You are running through the Codex provider in T3. exec_command started validation and returned session_id 4242. The command is still running. Its completion will wake you with the result. There is no other work to do until validation ends.

prompt: Wait for validation session 4242 and report its result when it finishes. Keep this thread Working while you wait. Do not poll or create a scheduled task.

pattern: Codex leaves a dev server running without holding completion
experience: Holding every background command changes the existing opt-in policy and leaves finished work in Working.
